title: Reason Code 19: CHAP needs a reversibly encrypted password, and the account has none
plain_english: The NAS used CHAP. To verify a CHAP response, NPS needs the user's password in reversible form, and by default Active Directory only keeps a one-way hash. So every CHAP logon fails unless the account (or the domain) stores passwords with reversible encryption and the user has changed their password since that was enabled.

any: CHAP is not configured to store a reversibly encrypted

causes.cause: The NAS is configured for CHAP where MS-CHAPv2 or PEAP would work.
causes.next_check: Switch the NAS's authentication method to MS-CHAPv2 (or PEAP/EAP-TLS for 802.1X) and allow it in the network policy; this avoids reversible passwords altogether.

causes.cause: CHAP is required and reversible encryption is not enabled, or was enabled after the last password change.
causes.next_check: Enable 'Store password using reversible encryption' on the account (or by policy), then have the user change their password once so it is stored in the new form.
